C-BROWSER-DEVTOOLS-DIAGNOSTICS-20260903.Summary:
Deliver the next bounded M1.3 browser-service slice by adding a replaceable, engine-neutral diagnostics capability above the browser provider and proving it against the real CEF path.
The primary product of this change is not a second Chrome DevTools frontend and not a raw Chromium debugging tunnel. The primary product is a Worldline diagnostic boundary that can expose bounded, page-scoped console, network and runtime observations to authorized consumers without coupling shell, agents or future tooling to CEF/CDP implementation details.
A small `worldline-browser-devtools` service plugin is the first proving consumer/owner of normalized diagnostic state. CEF remains responsible only for extracting engine facts through maintained callbacks or other explicitly bounded provider mechanisms. A provider-native DevTools window may exist as an optional high-trust escape hatch, but it is not the Worldline contract and does not grant raw debugging authority to ordinary diagnostic observers.
C-BROWSER-DEVTOOLS-DIAGNOSTICS-20260903.Problem:
Worldline now has a real browser engine provider, browser service plugins, durable downloads/cookies, and a bounded request-policy interception path, but operational browser diagnosis is still primarily an engineering activity: repository tests, provider logs and direct knowledge of CEF internals are required to understand console failures, resource failures and browser/runtime state.
That is insufficient for the upcoming shell and later agent/runtime work. A shell diagnostics surface, a support workflow, or an authorized agent should be able to ask what happened on a page without depending on a CEF pointer, Chromium DevTools Protocol object, remote debugging port, provider-local log file or ad hoc parsing of process stdout.
Exposing raw CDP or embedding Chrome DevTools as the canonical Worldline API would make diagnostics engine-specific, would grant far more mutation power than many observers need, and would make future browser-engine replacement expensive. Conversely, pushing every console/network item through the generic event bus as an unbounded firehose would create avoidable volume, privacy and lifecycle problems and would blur the distinction between observation, transport and persistence.
Worldline therefore needs a bounded browser diagnostics service with explicit authority, lifecycle ownership, privacy boundaries, truncation semantics and real-provider evidence, while preserving browser availability when the diagnostics plugin is absent, overloaded, crashed or replaced.

Goals.Goal: Define an additive experimental `browser.devtools/0.1` service contract for engine-neutral browser diagnostics without changing stable Browser Contract v1.0 semantics.

Introduce only the minimal experimental engine/provider diagnostics seam needed to supply the service with normalized console, network and page/runtime observations; no CEF or CDP type may cross that seam.
Implement one ordinary replaceable `worldline-browser-devtools` plugin that owns bounded ephemeral diagnostic buffers and query/control behavior above the engine provider.
Capture structured console observations sufficient to distinguish at least normal log/info, warning and error records together with safe source/location metadata when the engine supplies it reliably.

Capture bounded network/resource lifecycle observations sufficient to show request identity within a page, method, resource type, URL under authorized scope, completion/failure status, HTTP status where available, MIME type and bounded timing/size metadata where the engine can supply them reliably.

Provide a bounded page/runtime diagnostic snapshot that can identify the BrowserContextId, PageId, DocumentRevision, loading/navigation state and provider/renderer health facts already available through approved browser boundaries without leaking platform handles or privileged process internals.
Keep diagnostic observation authority separate from diagnostic control and from any optional provider-native DevTools authority.
Prove exact BrowserContextId/PageId isolation, lifecycle cleanup, bounded retention, overflow/truncation reporting and failure isolation.

Add a deterministic S3D proving slice and a real hosted Windows CEF path in which a loopback page emits known console records and known successful and failing resources that are visible through the normal Worldline diagnostics service path.
Preserve the ability to replace CEF later without rewriting diagnostic consumers, shell surfaces, agents or the kernel.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL AND EXACT PLAN APPROVAL ARE SEPARATE. THIS DRAFT DOES NOT AUTHORIZE IMPLEMENTATION.
C-BROWSER-REQUEST-POLICY-INTERCEPTION-SCOPE-CORRECTION-20260902 MUST BE APPLIED AND ARCHIVED BEFORE THIS CHANGE'S PLAN IS APPROVED OR EXECUTED.
DEVTOOLS/DIAGNOSTICS IS AN ORDINARY REPLACEABLE BROWSER SERVICE. NO DEVTOOLS, CONSOLE, NETWORK-INSPECTOR, CDP OR CEF-SPECIFIC DOMAIN POLICY MAY ENTER `worldline-kernel`.

THE WORLDLINE CONTRACT MUST BE ENGINE-NEUTRAL. CEF OBJECTS, CHROMIUM/CDP TYPES, HWND, RAW POINTERS, PROVIDER-LOCAL FILE PATHS, SOCKET HANDLES AND PLATFORM-SPECIFIC DEBUGGER OBJECTS MUST NOT CROSS THE CONTRACT OR IPC BOUNDARY.
RAW CHROME DEVTOOLS PROTOCOL PASSTHROUGH IS NOT THE V0.1 WORLDLINE API. DO NOT EXPOSE A GENERIC `send_cdp(method, json)`-STYLE CAPABILITY AS THE PRIMARY IMPLEMENTATION OF THIS SLICE.

A REMOTE DEBUGGING SERVER/PORT MUST NOT BE ENABLED AS A DEFAULT PRODUCT OR TEST REQUIREMENT FOR THIS SLICE. ANY FUTURE REMOTE DEBUGGING EXPOSURE REQUIRES A SEPARATE SECURITY DESIGN AND EXPLICIT AUTHORITY MODEL.

AN OPTIONAL PROVIDER-NATIVE DEVTOOLS WINDOW, IF IMPLEMENTED, IS A SEPARATE HIGH-TRUST CONTROL CAPABILITY. POSSESSION OF DIAGNOSTIC OBSERVATION AUTHORITY MUST NOT IMPLY AUTHORITY TO OPEN NATIVE DEVTOOLS, EXECUTE JAVASCRIPT, MUTATE DOM, CHANGE STORAGE OR OTHERWISE CONTROL THE PAGE.
DIAGNOSTIC OBSERVATION AUTHORITY MUST BE SCOPED TO BrowserContextId AND, WHERE APPLICABLE, PageId. A PRINCIPAL AUTHORIZED FOR CONTEXT/PAGE A MUST NOT OBSERVE DIAGNOSTICS FROM CONTEXT/PAGE B.

CONSOLE TEXT AND FULL REQUEST URLS ARE POTENTIALLY SENSITIVE. THEY MAY BE RETURNED ONLY TO AN AUTHORIZED DIAGNOSTIC PRINCIPAL FOR THE ADMITTED PAGE OR CONTEXT SCOPE AND MUST NOT BE COPIED INTO GENERIC METRICS, TRAJECTORY, PANIC TEXT OR UNRELATED EVENTS BY DEFAULT.

RAW Cookie/Authorization/Proxy-Authorization HEADER VALUES, CLIENT CERTIFICATE MATERIAL, REQUEST/RESPONSE BODIES, UPLOAD BYTES, FORM DATA, RESPONSE CONTENT AND ARBITRARY STORAGE VALUES ARE NOT PART OF THE DEFAULT DIAGNOSTIC DTOs IN THIS SLICE.

DIAGNOSTIC STORAGE IS BOUNDED AND EPHEMERAL BY DEFAULT. PERSISTING RAW CONSOLE OR NETWORK DATA REQUIRES A LATER EXPLICIT RECORDER/PERSISTENCE DESIGN WITH RETENTION, REDACTION AND AUTHORITY; EVENT PUBLICATION DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY MAKE DIAGNOSTICS DURABLE.
EVERY PER-PAGE/PER-CONTEXT BUFFER HAS FINITE ENTRY, BYTE AND FIELD-SIZE BOUNDS. OVERRUN MUST BE OBSERVABLE THROUGH DROP/TRUNCATION METADATA AND MUST NOT CREATE UNBOUNDED MEMORY GROWTH.

HIGH-VOLUME RAW DIAGNOSTIC DATA MUST NOT USE THE GENERIC EVENT BUS AS AN UNBOUNDED FIREHOSE. A METADATA-ONLY `updated`/`dropped` OBSERVATION MAY BE PUBLISHED IF USEFUL, BUT EVENT DELIVERY IS NOT A QUERY RESULT, NOT PERSISTENCE AND NOT AUTHORITY. EVENT BUS IS NOT RPC.

DIAGNOSTICS MUST NOT BLOCK NAVIGATION, NETWORK DISPATCH, CEF IO THREADS OR RENDERER PROGRESS ON A SLOW/FAILED DIAGNOSTICS CONSUMER. CAPTURE AND DELIVERY MECHANISMS MUST HAVE BOUNDED WORK AND BACKPRESSURE/DROP POLICY.

FAILURE, ABSENCE, UNLOAD, QUARANTINE OR RESTART OF THE OPTIONAL `worldline-browser-devtools` SERVICE MUST DEGRADE DIAGNOSTICS, NOT ORDINARY BROWSING OR UNRELATED TABS/HISTORY/DOWNLOADS/COOKIES/REQUEST-POLICY SERVICES.
DIAGNOSTIC ENTRIES MUST CARRY ENOUGH PAGE/DOCUMENT IDENTITY TO PREVENT A STALE RECORD FROM BEING MISREPRESENTED AS BELONGING TO A NEW DocumentRevision AFTER NAVIGATION.
STABLE Browser Contract v1.0 AND EXISTING EXPERIMENTAL ENGINE 0.1/0.2 AND request-policy/0.1 CONTRACTS MUST NOT BE INCOMPATIBLY REDEFINED. NEW DEVTOOLS/DIAGNOSTICS CONTRACTS START EXPERIMENTAL.

REAL CEF EVIDENCE MUST USE THE PINNED PRODUCTION PROVIDER PATH AND MUST REJECT ReferenceBrowserBackend SUBSTITUTION. REFERENCE FIXTURES MAY REMAIN AS SEPARATELY LABELLED DETERMINISTIC LOWER-LEVEL TESTS.

THE PLAN MUST INSPECT THE PINNED CEF BINDING AND SELECT MAINTAINED, THREAD-SAFE CALLBACKS OR PROVIDER MECHANISMS FOR CONSOLE/NETWORK FACTS. IF REQUIRED DATA CAN ONLY BE OBTAINED THROUGH AN UNBOUNDED RAW CDP TUNNEL, PUBLIC REMOTE DEBUGGING PORT OR UNSAFE CALLBACK LIFETIME, STOP AND REPLAN.
WINDOWS-FIRST CEF IMPLEMENTATION REMAINS BEHIND PLATFORM-NEUTRAL CONTRACTS. NON-WINDOWS WORKSPACE COMPILATION MUST REMAIN GREEN AND UNSUPPORTED NATIVE DEVTOOLS OPERATIONS MUST FAIL EXPLICITLY.
EXISTING M0, M1.1, M1.2, S3A, S3B, S3C, BrowserProvider, BrowserServices, BrowserRequestPolicy AND REAL-S3B GATES ARE NOT WEAKENED, SKIPPED OR REWRITTEN TO MAKE THIS CHANGE GREEN.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Building a full replacement for Chrome DevTools, Firefox DevTools or Edge DevTools.
Exposing raw CDP as Worldline's stable or primary diagnostics API.
Arbitrary JavaScript evaluation or a programmable page console.
DOM editing, CSS editing, element-inspector authoring tools or live style mutation.
Debugger breakpoints, stepping, source-map debugging or script instrumentation.
Heap snapshots, allocation profiling, CPU profiling or full performance tracing.
Response-body capture, HAR export, arbitrary request/response header capture or packet capture.
Persistent raw diagnostics history or cloud synchronization.
Worldline Shell or M1.4 renderer/compositor work.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A companion ADR documents the diagnostic contract, authority classes, sensitivity model, buffer/drop semantics, lifecycle behavior, CEF adapter boundary, native DevTools escape-hatch policy and rejected raw-CDP design.
An additive experimental `browser.devtools/0.1` service contract exists without changing stable Browser Contract v1.0 wire semantics.
Any new engine-side diagnostics primitive or provider callback contract is additive/experimental and contains only engine-neutral DTOs.

The service contract has separate authority for diagnostic observation and diagnostic control; any optional native DevTools/open-inspector authority is separate again and is never implied by ordinary page observation.
Possession of BrowserContextId, PageId, DocumentRevision, diagnostic cursor, entry ID or URL alone does not grant diagnostic access.
A diagnostic observer admitted for Context/Page A cannot query console, network or runtime diagnostics for Context/Page B, including when both use the same loopback origin.
Diagnostic records are associated with PageId and DocumentRevision where applicable so records from an old document are not silently presented as records from the current document after navigation.
Console observations support deterministic log/info, warning and error fixtures and preserve bounded message/source/location metadata supplied by the real engine.

Network observations support deterministic successful and failing resource fixtures and expose only the approved bounded metadata, including HTTP status/MIME/timing/size fields only where the real provider supplies them reliably.

Raw cookies, authorization credentials, client certificate material, request/response bodies, upload bytes and response content do not enter the default diagnostic DTOs, generic metrics, panic output or Debug output in the proving path.

Console/network field sizes and per-page/per-context retained entry counts are finite and tested. Oversized fields are rejected or explicitly truncated with metadata; buffer overflow increments a bounded drop/overflow counter rather than allocating without limit.
A deterministic flood fixture proves diagnostics remain bounded and the page remains usable while old/extra diagnostic entries are dropped according to the documented policy.

Diagnostic buffers are ephemeral by default and service restart does not make an accidental durability claim; a fresh runtime does not inherit stale authority or mutable handles from the previous runtime generation.
Page/context close and provider/service restart invalidate relevant live cursors/subscriptions/handles and no callback targets a dead RuntimeId.

The real CEF provider captures the required console/network facts before normalization using maintained pinned-binding callbacks or provider mechanisms selected by the approved plan, without a raw CDP passthrough in the Worldline contract.
No remote debugging port is required for the normal diagnostics proving path and no broadly reachable remote-debugging endpoint is enabled by the test fixture.

If an optional provider-native DevTools operation is implemented, it is capability-negotiated, separately authorized, fails explicitly when unsupported, and does not leak a CEF/browser handle to the caller.
The diagnostics plugin may be absent, unloaded, crashed, quarantined or replaced without failing ordinary navigation or unrelated browser services.

A metadata-only diagnostic-update event, if implemented, is observational only; the diagnostic query result is obtained through the explicit service contract and is not determined by an event subscriber.

A deterministic S3D reference fixture uses repository-owned loopback pages and proves console capture, success/failure network capture, exact scope, overflow semantics, lifecycle cleanup and failure isolation without public Internet dependencies.

A hosted Windows real-CEF S3D acceptance path uses the pinned native provider process and proves at least one known console marker, one warning or error, one successful loopback resource and one failed/404 loopback resource are observable through the Worldline diagnostics service.
Real S3D evidence records selected provider/runtime identity and rejects ReferenceBrowserBackend substitution as production proof.

Static architecture checks prove `worldline-kernel` contains no devtools, console-inspector, CDP or CEF diagnostic domain types and prove the `worldline-browser-devtools` service does not become a dependency of tabs, history, downloads, cookies or request-policy services.
Static architecture checks prove raw CEF/CDP/platform handles do not enter service contracts, IPC payloads or generic events.

A separately named BrowserDevTools CI suite covers contracts, authority isolation, bounds, lifecycle cleanup, failure isolation, deterministic S3D and the real hosted Windows CEF path; hosted real evidence fails closed when required pinned CEF staging variables are absent.

Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, ProvingSlice, RealChromium, BrowserProvider, BrowserServices, BrowserRequestPolicy, BrowserDevTools, RealS3B and All are green for the final implementation state, with local and hosted evidence reported separately.
Completion reporting distinguishes scaffolded contract/service files, wired real-provider diagnostic flow and verified named real-CEF evidence.
This change is neither transitioned to applied nor archived as successfully applied until fresh required evidence is green and the owner explicitly confirms GRACE apply.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh evidence names the experimental diagnostics contract revision, separate diagnostic authorities, bounded/drop semantics, privacy omissions, exact context/page/document isolation, real CEF console and network capture, optional native-DevTools authority behavior where implemented, failure isolation, deterministic and hosted S3D runs, architecture guards and a successful hosted master run. Local/reference and hosted real-browser evidence are reported separately.

Assumptions.Assumption: The current pinned CEF binding exposes maintained callbacks or provider mechanisms sufficient to obtain the minimal console and network facts in this spec without making raw CDP or a remote debugging server the Worldline contract; the approved plan must verify this assumption before relying on it.
Existing browser identity, lifecycle and authority vocabulary is sufficient to scope diagnostics without adding browser-specific privileged kernel state.
Bounded in-memory diagnostic buffers are sufficient for the first M1.3 proving slice; persistence and long-term support bundles can be designed later from measured use rather than assumed now.

Existing request-policy metadata may be reused where its semantics match a diagnostic fact, but diagnostics do not depend on adblock policy execution and do not gain interception authority through that reuse.

A provider-native DevTools window is useful as an operator escape hatch but is not required to define the neutral diagnostic service; the plan may keep it optional if deterministic automated evidence cannot prove it without expanding security scope.
Search providers, crypto/trust compatibility and M1.4 shell composition remain separate changes after this bounded diagnostics slice.
